SIRT4 over‐expression enhances the tamoxifene sensitivity of breast cancer by inhibiting the activation of the STAT3 signalling pathway, which is a potential new target for breast cancer treatment.

sirtuin 1 enhances the sensitivity of estrogen receptor‐positive MCF7 and ER‐positive breast T47D cells to tamoxifene, and that this is achieved by inhibiting the activation of the IL‐6/JAK2/STAT3 signal transduction pathway.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of SIRT4 in breast cancer cells and the molecular mechanism of its effect on tamoxifen sensitivity.
the biological role of SIRT4 in tamoxifen resistance.
the role of SIRT4 in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SIRT4 can enhance the sensitivity of breast tumors to endocrine therapy by inhibiting the activation of the STAT3 signal pathway.

the SIRT4/STAT3 axis plays a critical role in breast cancer cell tamoxifen sensitivity, providing new insights into the mechanism underlying the development of tamoxifen resistance and a new therapeutic strategy for the treatment of breast cancer.

sirtuin 3 (SIRT3) enhances the sensitivity of tamoxifen‐positive breast cancer cells to treatment by inhibiting the interleukin‐6 (IL‐6)/signal transducer and activators of transcription (STAT) 3 signal pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) is a tumor suppressor in breast cancer, and sirtuin 3 (SIRT3) is an oncogene.
the sirtuin 1 and 4 (SIR1 and SIR4) genes were up‐regulated and SIR4 expression was positively correlated with the estrogen receptor (ER) status in breast cancer tissues.
sirtuin 5 is an important molecule in regulating the sensitivity of breast tumor cells to tamoxifene, and it can be used as a new target for the treatment of estrogen receptor‐positive tumors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

SIRT4 can enhance the tamoxifen‐sensitivity of breast cancer cells, and this effect is achieved by inhibiting the activation of STAT3, which in turn suppresses the transcription of MYC and the translation of CCND1.
SIRT4 can enhance the sensitivity of estrogen‐receptor‐positive breast cancer cells to the anti‐estrogen tamoxifen by suppressing the STAT3 pathway.
SIRT4 can be used to increase the sensitivity of estrogen receptor‐positive cancer cells to tamaxifen, thereby reducing drug resistance.
